readings.title: Saul's Disobedience
readings.subtitle: The War Against Amaleq
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:1] And Shemu’el said to Sha’ul, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent me to anoint you sovereign over <dn>His</dn> people, over Yisra’el. And now, listen to the voice of the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> shall punish Amaleq for what he did to Yisra’el, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Mitsrayim.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Now go, and you shall smite Amaleq and put to the ban all that he has, and you shall not spare them, and you shall put to death from man to woman, from child to nursing infant, from ox to sheep, from camel to donkey.’</dq> ” [4] And Sha’ul summoned the people and inspected them in Tela’im, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Yehuḏah. [5] And Sha’ul came to a city of Amaleq, and lay in wait in the valley. [6] And Sha’ul said to the Qeynite, “Go, depart, go down from among the Amaleqites, lest I destroy you with them. For you showed kindness to all the children of Yisra’el when they came up out of Mitsrayim.” So the Qeynite departed from among the Amaleqites. [7] And Sha’ul smote the Amaleqites, from Ḥawilah all the way to Shur, which is east of Mitsrayim. [8] And he caught Aḡaḡ sovereign of the Amaleqites alive, and put all the people to the ban with the edge of the sword. [9] But Sha’ul and the people spared Aḡaḡ and the best of the sheep, and the cattle, and the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and were not willing to put them to the ban. But all livestock that was despised and worthless, that they put to the ban.

readings.title: To Obey is Better than Sacrifice
readings.subtitle: Samuel Confronts Saul
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:10] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shemu’el, saying, [11] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am grieved that <dn>I</dn> have set up Sha’ul as sovereign, for he has turned back from following <dn>Me</dn>, and has not performed <dn>My</dn> words.”</dq> And it displeased Shemu’el, and he cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all night. [12] And Shemu’el rose early in the morning to meet Sha’ul, and it was reported to Shemu’el, saying, “Sha’ul went to Karmel, and see, he set up a monument for himself, and has turned and passed over, and has gone down to Gilḡal.” [13] And Shemu’el came to Sha’ul, and Sha’ul said to him, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! I have performed the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [14] But Shemu’el said, “What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the lowing of the cattle which I hear?” [15] And Sha’ul said, “They have brought them from the Amaleqites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle, to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the rest we have put to the ban.” [16] And Shemu’el said to Sha’ul, “Wait, and let me declare to you what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me last night.” And he said to him, “Speak.” [17] And Shemu’el said, “Though you were little in your own eyes, were you not the head of the tribes of Yisra’el? And did not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> anoint you sovereign over Yisra’el? [18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent you on the way, and said, <dq>‘Go, and you shall put to the ban the sinners, the Amaleqites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’</dq> [19] “And why did you not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but swooped down on the spoil, and did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [20] And Sha’ul said to Shemu’el, “I did obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and went on the way on which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent me, and brought back Aḡaḡ sovereign of Amaleq, and I have put the Amaleqites to the ban. [21] “But the people took of the spoil, of the sheep and cattle, the chief of the banned things, to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in Gilḡal.” [22] And Shemu’el said, “Does <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> delight in burnt offerings and slaughterings, as in obeying the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Look, to obey is better than slaughtering, to give heed is better than the fat of rams. [23] “For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as wickedness and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> also has rejected you from being sovereign.”

readings.title: The Kingdom Torn
readings.subtitle: The Rejection of Saul and Death of Agag
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:24] And Sha’ul said to Shemu’el, “I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and your words, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice. [25] “And now, please pardon my sin, and return with me, and let me bow myself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [26] But Shemu’el said to Sha’ul, “I do not return with you, for you have rejected the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rejected you from being sovereign over Yisra’el.” [27] And as Shemu’el turned around to go, he seized the edge of his robe, and it tore. [28] And Shemu’el said to him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has torn the reign of Yisra’el from you today, and has given it to a neighbor of yours, better than you. [29] “And also the Pre-eminence of Yisra’el does not lie nor relent, for <dn>He</dn> is not a man, that <dn>He</dn> should relent.” [30] And he said, “I have sinned, yet honor me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Yisra’el, and return with me, and I shall bow myself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [31] And Shemu’el returned after Sha’ul, and Sha’ul bowed himself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [32] And Shemu’el said, “Bring Aḡaḡ sovereign of the Amaleqites here to me.” So Aḡaḡ came to him hesitantly. And Aḡaḡ said, “Truly the bitterness of death has turned aside.” [33] And Shemu’el said, “As your sword has made women bereaved, so is your mother bereaved among women.” And Shemu’el hewed Aḡaḡ in pieces before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Gilḡal. [34] And Shemu’el went to Ramah, and Sha’ul went up to his house at Giḇʽah of Sha’ul. [35] And Shemu’el did not see Sha’ul again until the day of his death, for Shemu’el mourned for Sha’ul. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented that <dn>He</dn> had made Sha’ul sovereign over Yisra’el.

readings.title: The Anointing of David
readings.subtitle: Man Looks at the Outward Appearance
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’el, <dq>“How long are you going to mourn for Sha’ul, seeing <dn>I</dn> have rejected him from reigning over Yisra’el? Fill your horn with oil, and go, <dn>I</dn> am sending you to Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite. For <dn>I</dn> have seen among his sons a sovereign for <dn>Myself</dn>.”</dq> [2] And Shemu’el said, “How do I go? When Sha’ul hears it, he shall kill me.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘I have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq> [3] <dq>“And you shall invite Yishai to the slaughtering, and <dn>I</dn> make known to you what you do, and you shall anoint for <dn>Me</dn> the one <dn>I</dn> say to you.”</dq> [4] And Shemu’el did what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, and went to Běyth Leḥem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, “Do you come in peace?” [5] And he said, “In peace. I have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Set yourselves apart, and you shall come with me to the slaughtering.” And he set Yishai and his sons apart, and invited them to the slaughtering. [6] And it came to be, when they came, that he saw Eliyaḇ, and said, “Surely <dn>His</dn> anointed is before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [7] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’el, <dq>“Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because <dn>I</dn> have refused him. For not as man sees, for man looks at the outward appearance, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looks at the heart.”</dq> [8] Then Yishai called Aḇinaḏaḇ, and made him pass before Shemu’el. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [9] Then Yishai made Shammah pass by. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [10] And Yishai made seven of his sons pass before Shemu’el. And Shemu’el said to Yishai, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not chosen these.” [11] And Shemu’el said to Yishai, “Are these all the youths?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, and see, he is tending the sheep.” And Shemu’el said to Yishai, “Send and bring him. For we do not turn round until he comes here.” [12] And he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with bright eyes, and good looking. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Arise, anoint him, for this is the one!”</dq> [13] And Shemu’el took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Dawiḏ from that day forward. And Shemu’el arose and went to Ramah.

readings.title: David in Saul's Court
readings.subtitle: The Spirit of YeHoVaH Departs from Saul
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:14] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned aside from Sha’ul, and an evil spirit from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> troubled him. [15] And Sha’ul’s servants said to him, “Look, please, an evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is troubling you. [16] “Please let our master command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is a skilled player on the lyre. And it shall be that he plays with his hand when the evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is upon you, and you shall be well.” [17] And Sha’ul said to his servants, “Please provide me a man who plays well, and bring him to me.” [18] And one of the servants answered and said, “Look, I have seen a son of Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite, who understands playing, and is a mighty brave man, a man of battle, and speaks intelligently, and is a handsome man. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with him.” [19] And Sha’ul sent messengers to Yishai, and said, “Send me your son Dawiḏ, who is with the sheep.” [20] And Yishai took a donkey loaded with bread, and a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by his son Dawiḏ to Sha’ul. [21] And Dawiḏ came to Sha’ul and stood before him. And he loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer. [22] And Sha’ul sent to Yishai, saying, “Please let Dawiḏ stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.” [23] And it came to be, whenever the spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon Sha’ul, that Dawiḏ would take a lyre and play it with his hand. Then Sha’ul would become refreshed and well, and the evil spirit would leave him.

readings.title: The Philistine Challenge
readings.subtitle: Goliath of Gath
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:1] And the Philistines gathered their armies for battle, and they were gathered at Sokoh, which belongs to Yehuḏah. And they encamped between Sokoh and Azěqah, in Ephes Dammim. [2] And Sha’ul and the men of Yisra’el were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and drew up in battle array to meet the Philistines. [3] And the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, and Yisra’el stood on a mountain on the other side, with a valley between them. [4] And a champion went out from the camp of the Philistines, named Golyath, from Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span. [5] And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was armed with a scale armor, and the weight of the coat was five thousand sheqels of bronze. [6] And bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze javelin between his shoulders. [7] And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and his iron spearhead weighed six hundred sheqels, and a shield-bearer went before him. [8] And he stood and cried out to the armies of Yisra’el, and said to them, “Why do you come out to draw up in battle array? Am I not a Philistine, and you the servants of Sha’ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me. [9] “If he is able to fight with me and beat me, then we shall be your servants. But if I prevail against him and beat him, then you shall be our servants and serve us.” [10] And the Philistine said, “I defy the armies of Yisra’el this day; give me a man that we might fight together.” [11] And Sha’ul and all Yisra’el heard these words of the Philistine, and they were broken down and greatly afraid.

readings.title: David Arrives at the Camp
readings.subtitle: David Hears the Challenge
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:12] Now Dawiḏ was the son of that Ephrathite of Běyth Leḥem of Yehuḏah, whose name was Yishai, and who had eight sons. And the man was old, advanced in years, in the days of Sha’ul. [13] And the three oldest sons of Yishai had gone to follow Sha’ul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliyaḇ the firstborn, and the second to him Aḇinaḏaḇ, and the third Shammah. [14] And Dawiḏ was the youngest. And the three oldest followed Sha’ul. [15] And Dawiḏ went and returned from Sha’ul to feed his father’s sheep at Běyth Leḥem. [16] And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and took his stand for forty days. [17] And Yishai said to his son Dawiḏ, “Take now for your brothers an ěphah of this dried grain and these ten loaves, and run to your brothers at the camp. [18] “And take these ten cheeses to the commander of their thousand, and look into the welfare of your brothers, and take their pledge.” [19] And Sha’ul and they and all the men of Yisra’el were in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines. [20] And Dawiḏ rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took and went as Yishai had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the fight and shouting for the battle. [21] And Yisra’el and the Philistines drew up in battle array, army against army. [22] And Dawiḏ left his supplies in the hand of the keeper of the supplies, and ran to the army, and came and asked his brothers about their welfare. [23] And as he spoke with them, look, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Golyath by name, coming up from the armies of the Philistines. And he spoke according to the same words. And Dawiḏ heard. [24] And all the men of Yisra’el, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid. [25] And the men of Yisra’el said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? For he has come up to defy Yisra’el. And it shall be, that the man who beats him the sovereign is going to enrich him with great riches, and give him his daughter, and give his father’s house exemption in Yisra’el.” [26] And Dawiḏ spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What is done for the man who beats this Philistine and takes away reproach from Yisra’el? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>?” [27] And the people answered him according to this word, saying, “So it is done for the man who beats him.” [28] And Eliyaḇ his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And the displeasure of Eliyaḇ burned against Dawiḏ, and he said, “Why did you come down here? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.” [29] And Dawiḏ said, “What have I done now? Is there not a cause?” [30] And he turned from him toward another and spoke according to the same word. And the people answered him a word again like the first word. [31] And the words which Dawiḏ spoke were heard, and they reported them to Sha’ul, and he took him.
